messages:
anna: quick heads-up — canary for mb_policy=v2 (mb_target=2 for streaming) is showing a p99 spike on chat-route (~2100ms -> ~3400ms). noticed right after the kernel hint change that prefers kernel-x86-optim for short sequences.

devon: ugh. timeline? did this correlate with traffic pattern change or a config push?

anna: config push at 08:12 UTC (canary). deploy-bot reports rollout completed. traffic steady (~10qps), but tail moves only on streaming chat. non-stream completions don't regress.

deploy-bot: rollout: canary mb_policy=v2 completed (service/runtime-host-12).

mike: interesting that completions unaffected. suggests per-token work or KV-cache warmup differences. streaming does prefix sends + handshake overhead. any traces?

anna: got profile traces from canary host. short summary: p50 similar, p95 up a bit, p99 doubled. kernel selection changed for short sequences which increased tail CPU stalls. here is a snippet from perf trace (sampled wall time per op):

```
kernel-x86-optim: mean 0.45ms/token, tail 3.1ms/token (samples show occasional 12ms stalls)
kernel-gpu-default: mean 0.6ms/token, tail 0.9ms/token
KV lookup (miss) latency: mean 0.9ms, tail 4.8ms
Batching queue wait (mb_target=2): median 3ms, p99 150ms
```

devon: those batching queue p99s look bad. when mb=2 we might be forcing small batches that increase scheduling overhead and amplify KV miss tail. are we still doing prefix-level KV prefetch for streaming?

anna: yes, prefetch=on for streaming. but prefetch gets invalidated more often with kernel-x86 because of different memory layout — increases eviction churn. looks like KV cache churn -> more misses -> occasional long stalls.

sarah: could also be kernel's memory allocator causing hiccups. kernel-x86 uses jemalloc variant with different background threads. If throttled, it shows as 10-20ms stalls. do we have stack traces for those 12ms samples?

mike: i pulled a few async stacks. most show: 

```
poll_wait -> kv_cache_lookup -> memcpy -> kernel-x86-optim::attention_fast_path -> futex_wait
```

mike: pattern suggests serialization at KV path when several microbatches hit the same shard. mb_target=2 reduces batching headroom, so collisions more visible.

devon: what's current routing? are we collapsing streaming+nonstream into same pool? might be worthwhile to split into separate pools where kernel selection differs.

anna: can try split-pool canary. but before that i want to test two quick mitigations: 1) disable kernel-x86 hint for short seqs to force kernel-gpu-default, 2) increase mb_target to 4 for streaming to give batching more headroom.

sarah: +1 to quick A/B. also add a KV cache metric for eviction rate per-second to dashboards. current dashboards only show miss rate but not eviction churn.

devon: agreed. run both as parallel canaries: kernel-hint-off and mb_target=4. run 1h each, compare p99, KV eviction/sec, and batch wait p99.

anna: started canaries. kernel-hint-off -> canary-id kco-1715-1, mb4 -> canary-id mb4-1715-2. traffic split 5% each. logs/trace links: https://perf.internal/canaries/1715

deploy-bot: canary kco-1715-1 deployed to host-21.

mike: quick note — when increasing mb_target, need to watch streaming handshake latency impact (first byte). we might improve tail but hurt first-byte latency. include first-byte p50/p95 in checks.

anna: good call. i've instrumented first_byte_{p50,p95}. will collect for 30m then report.

(30 minutes later)

anna: results after 30m: kco-1715-1 (kernel-hint-off): chat p99 -> 980ms (vs 3400ms), KV eviction/sec down 6x, batch wait p99 40ms. mb4-1715-2: chat p99 -> 1200ms, first_byte_p50 unchanged, first_byte_p95 +18ms.

devon: so both help, kernel-hint-off best. mb4 helps but with small first-byte penalty.

sarah: kernel-hint-off seems safe as immediate rollback. but we should dig into why kernel-x86 triggers eviction churn. maybe its allocator alignment/padding increasing memory working set.

mike: next steps: 1) rollback hint in canary -> propagate to prod after another hour 2) reproduce locally with stress test that simulates streaming microbatch=2 and KV shard collisions 3) add eviction/sec metric and KV per-shard histograms 4) investigate kernel allocator config and consider patch to reduce background GC pauses.

devon: also add a safety that streaming routes prefer kernels with stable tail-latency for small mb sizes. we can keep kernel-x86-optim for heavy-bulk completions but avoid for short streaming sequences.

anna: agreed. i'll open the rollout PR with proposed immediate rollback and the routing policy change. cc @devon @mike for review.

anna: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4823

mike: nice work. once PR merges let's run a long soak to see if the regression fully disappears at scale. :thumbsup:

devon: and add an alert for batch_wait_p99 > 300ms for streaming routes — sounded like a good sentinel for mb-induced tail spikes.

sarah: adding eviction/sec chart to runtime console. will post link when live.

anna: thanks all — rolling this to prod in ~90m if no surprises.

deploy-bot: rollback: kernel-hint-off applied to canary group, pending promotion to prod after soak.

anna: closing the loop: after 3h soak, prod p99 back to baseline. followups created: #ticket-PR-4823 (routing policy), #ticket-OBS-771 (eviction metrics), #ticket-ALLOC-209 (allocator investigation).

devon: great. extra note: document the microbatch tradeoffs in the runtime handbook — small mb reduces latency for steady streams but can amplify tail from KV collisions and allocator hiccups.

anna: adding a short doc patch now.

sarah: :celebrate:
